# Lanesra OS — Detailed Product Context

Lanesra OS is an independent, open-source, AI-native business application platform for organizations that need more structure than spreadsheets but don't want the licensing cost, lock-in or complexity of enterprise CRM/ERP/integration platforms. It leads with (1) an AI Agent Foundry and Unified AI Gateway - named agents with persona, Actions, Memory, Skills and delegation, orchestrated into deterministic Pipelines and triggered runs, routed through a Unified AI Gateway (bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible/Google Gemini key, or route to a fully local/air-gapped model, with automatic failover and token budgets), plus a Chat Assistant - where agents run directly against your real data, not a bolted-on chatbot with its own separate context pipeline; and (2) a native Model Context Protocol server & CLI that expose that same data to Claude Desktop, an IDE agent, or any MCP-capable client. Both sit on (3) a no-code platform - Custom Objects, Custom Relationships, Screen/App Builder, Business Rules, Workflow Automation, Dashboards, Reports - for building whatever business an organization actually runs, from that same settings screen, no developer required - which also powers (4) a complete CRM out of the box, the Business OS everything above runs against, and (5) an Industry Data Model - a versioned package manifest format plus an App Catalog of 11 ready-made industry apps to install instead of building from scratch, plus a Lanesra Industry Foundation package (desktop only) of shared cross-industry objects - Party, Party Role, Party Relationship, Location, Asset, Agreement and more - other packages can optionally declare a real, enforced dependency on and relate to instead of reinventing. On top of that sit (6) Deployment Management - Publishers, versioned Solutions, component export/import, update-with-diff - for packaging and promoting customizations from a test workspace to production the way a real software vendor would, without enterprise licensing; and (7) an Integration Hub - encrypted Connections, OpenAPI Connectors, a generic REST API, HMAC-signed Webhooks, CSV data exchange, scheduled Integration Jobs - for connecting Lanesra to every other system a business already runs.

## Product status

The product is currently in Early Access. The desktop app itself is at v0.12.0; the website/product tracks a separate sequential version counter, now at v0.45.0. Beyond the CRM core described below, the desktop edition (Tauri + Rust + SQLite) now ships a full application-platform stack. The no-code layer - Custom Objects, Custom Relationships, Screen/App Builder, Business Rules, Workflow Automation, custom Dashboards and Reports - lets an Administrator define an entirely new record type at runtime (Vendors, Assets, Projects, …), connect it to anything else with a chosen cardinality, lay out its create/edit and detail screens by role, and drive conditional logic and automation across any field, built-in or custom. On top of that, App Builder groups any set of objects, their published screens and a dashboard into a named, publishable app with role/user-based Viewer/Editor access enforced server-side on every write (including status-lifecycle actions like issuing an invoice or converting a quote to an order), and the App Catalog installs one of ten ready-made industry reference packages - Field Service, Property Management, Construction & Contractors, Professional Services, Dental/Clinic Practice Administration, Recruitment & Staffing, Real Estate Brokerage, Legal Practice, Nonprofit & Association Management, and Auto Repair & Service Garage - each with pre-install validation, an automatic safety backup, and a transactional, rollback-safe install that reuses the workspace's existing Company/Contact/Task records rather than creating a parallel data model.

Deployment Management sits on top of that: a Publisher registry enforces namespace ownership over a package's identifier, every admin-configurable artifact (objects, fields, relationships, business rules, workflows, screens, reports, dashboards) is tagged to the component that created it - hand-built or installed - so a "Local Workspace" view shows everything built by hand, distinct from what an installed app created. An admin can curate a named, versioned Solution from any subset of that workspace's components, export it to a manifest file, and import it into a second workspace through the same validated, backed-up, transactional pipeline the App Catalog uses - the build-in-test, promote-to-production pattern enterprise platforms charge for, running here on ordinary export/import between two self-hosted instances. Once a newer version of an installed package is imported, update-with-diff previews exactly what changed (objects/fields get a real per-key Added/Modified/Removed diff; everything else a summarized added-count) before the update is applied.

The Integration Hub is the newest layer, shipped on the desktop edition: Connections (generic REST, SFTP, PostgreSQL, OData, SMTP) with secrets encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM and a real Test Connection call; Connectors that import an OpenAPI 3.x spec and derive reusable Actions, each callable as a new Workflow Automation "Call Connector Action" step; API Access issuing hashed, scoped `{client_id}.{secret}` bearer keys against a real generic `/api/v1/objects/...` REST API on the Team Workspace server (a pure desktop install has no listening socket for an external caller to reach); Webhooks that sign every delivery with HMAC-SHA256, retry with exponential backoff, and keep a full delivery history; a Data Exchange wizard that generalizes what used to be a Companies/Contacts-only CSV import into an object-agnostic tool (any built-in or Custom Object, column mapping with transforms, duplicate/upsert policy, dry-run preview) routed through the same generic record-write path the REST API itself uses, so validation, business rules and permissions apply identically; External Objects surfacing read-only live records from a Connection; and Integration Jobs adding a recurring pull-sync on an interval with a checkpoint cursor, run by a real background scheduler thread on the Team Workspace server (desktop has no long-running process to host one, so a manual "Run Now" is the only way a desktop-hosted Job runs today). A unified execution log spans API calls, webhook deliveries and import/export runs, with a real KPI Overview and a Server-Sent-Events endpoint for live streaming. Best-effort, explicitly-labeled coverage beyond that core scope: SFTP and PostgreSQL connectors proven against a real in-process SFTP server and a real local Postgres instance, OAuth2 client-credentials and authorization-code token exchange against a mock endpoint, a minimal SMTP action, and an OData v4 query/response layer - mTLS is the one deliberate, named gap the spec itself marks as future work.

The public browser demo mirrors the entire no-code platform, the full 10-app App Catalog, and Deployment Management (Publishers, named Solutions with real export, Components, Dependencies) as real interactive features, not just changelog copy. Its Integration Hub section is relabeled to match the desktop feature's terminology and structure (Overview, Integration Jobs, API Access, Connections, Webhooks & Events) but stays an explicit UI-only simulation - the static demo has no server to make a real network call, encrypt a secret, sign a webhook payload, or run a real schedule, and its copy says so plainly rather than implying parity it doesn't have. The Windows desktop application itself is in early development: the source is public today, with the full sales lifecycle working end to end - Companies, Contacts, Products, Opportunities, Quotes, Orders and Invoices, including quote-to-order and order-to-invoice conversion, atomic document numbering and local user authentication - plus Contracts, Tasks, user management, Team Workspace mode for small teams (Docker), whole-workspace backup and restore, self-service password change, PDF generation and printing, and CSV import/export. There is no signed installer yet; desktop-v0.12.0 is the latest tagged Early Access Windows installer on GitHub Releases (unsigned), or build and run from source.

Saved Views & Bulk Actions followed that: any list screen that already supports filtering can save its current filter/sort/group-by combination as a named view - Private or Shared, with an admin-settable object default on the desktop edition - and reuse that view as a dashboard record-list widget's data source, narrowing the tile to exactly that subset instead of every record. Bulk operations pair with the multi-select a saved view narrows to: update a status/stage (validated through the same Status Transition rules a single edit already goes through), reassign owner, tag, and archive, each offered only where the underlying entity actually carries that field. Shipped on the desktop edition (Rust core: migration 0034, `saved_view_service`, `bulk_action_service`) and mirrored in the online demo against its simpler status-and-owner field set, without a Private/Shared distinction or a per-custom-field filter, since the demo has neither a signed-in-user concept nor desktop's per-field list filtering to begin with.

The newest layer on top of all of this is the AI & Agentic Layer, built in five phases. First, a bring-your-own-key LLM setting (Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint) powers a Chat Assistant with real tool access to records (any authenticated user) or the admin configuration surface (Administrators), plus a native Model Context Protocol server and CLI so an external MCP-capable client (Claude Desktop, an IDE agent) can reach the same records and business logic over JSON-RPC 2.0, authenticated with the same scoped API keys the REST API already uses. Second, the AI Agent Foundry: an Administrator defines named, reusable AI Agents - a persona layered over a per-tool Actions checklist (any admin-catalog action makes the agent Administrator-only, computed at runtime), a persistent Memory document the agent revises itself via its own tool, a shared Skills library (short description shown up front, full instructions loaded only on demand), and delegation to other agents, depth-guarded against runaway recursion. Third, Orchestration: agents chain into a deterministic, admin-authored Pipeline where each step's input can reference the previous step's real output; a Pipeline or lone Agent fires manually, on a schedule, from an authenticated webhook, or as a new "Run AI agent" Workflow Automation action, with every run - whatever triggered it - landing in one unified history. Fourth, the Unified AI Gateway: named, admin-managed AI Providers beyond a single workspace default, per-agent model routing across primary/fallback/local-fallback tiers with automatic failover, real per-(workspace, agent, user, day) token-usage accounting enforced against System- and Agent-level daily budgets, and DLP-driven forced air-gapping - a request touching a configured sensitive-data class (SSN, credit card number, and so on) routes straight to the local-fallback tier regardless of the normal order. Fifth, a Context Layer: real history for an agent's Memory (every prior value is snapshotted before being overwritten, whether by the agent's own tool or an admin's direct edit, so what an agent has "learned" over time is auditable and reviewable) and a SQLite FTS5-backed `search_records` tool giving agents ranked full-text search over Custom Object records - `bm25()` lexical relevance, matching the same self-hosted-on-SQLite philosophy the rest of the product already commits to. All five phases shipped on the desktop edition and are mirrored in the online demo. Five more pieces followed. An agent's own `guardrails_md` is injected into its system prompt as an explicit operational-boundary statement an admin can edit in either edition; on the desktop edition only, since it needs a real tool-calling loop, the loop itself also aborts with a clear error the moment the same `(tool, arguments)` call repeats 3 times in a row. Two more orchestration topologies alongside sequential - `consensus` (every step but the last runs independently, then a synthesizer combines every candidate's real answer) and `peer_review` (a drafter/reviewer loop bounded at 3 rounds) - and human-in-the-loop approval gates, extended from sequential Pipelines to every topology's own well-defined resume point (a consensus pipeline's synthesizer, a peer-review pipeline's reviewer every round), are both mirrored in the online demo too - a synchronous `confirm()` dialog standing in for the desktop's real persisted pause-and-resume. Desktop only: declarative export/import of an agent or Skill (persona, Memory seed, guardrails, Actions, Skills, delegates) as part of a Solution, reusing the existing Solution/package manifest mechanism rather than a parallel directory-of-files format; a real Evaluation Harness (`ai_eval_service`) - a named Suite of golden test Cases, each graded by an LLM-as-judge call rather than a brittle exact-match; OTLP tracing, where a finished run renders as a standard `resourceSpans` trace, exportable as JSON or pushed on demand to a configured collector endpoint; and an agent context primer, where `get_object_metadata` now lists every Custom Relationship an object participates in from either direction, a new `get_related_records` tool follows one for a specific record, and a new `get_platform_overview` tool explains how Lanesra OS's own primitives compose plus a live per-workspace summary. On top of that (desktop only, opt-in), Vector Search adds a genuinely-semantic second ranking - `semantic_search_records` - via real embeddings from the workspace's own already-configured OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini provider (Anthropic has no embeddings API), stored as plain SQLite BLOBs and ranked by brute-force cosine similarity in Rust rather than a bundled vector database or native extension; a synchronous SQL trigger can't call the provider, so a record's own create/update/archive only ever enqueues a reindex, drained asynchronously alongside every other queued agent work.

## Product history

- May 2026: Product idea and vision defined.
- June 2026: Architecture, scope and offline strategy established.
- July 2026: Design system and web MVP built.
- August 2026: Public Early Access launched.
- August 2026: Windows desktop edition foundation published (Tauri + SQLite, full sales lifecycle), followed within the month by Contracts, Tasks, user management, Team Workspace mode, backup/restore, self-service password change, PDF generation/printing, and CSV import/export.
- August 2026: An admin-configurable layer shipped on top of the fixed schema - branding and print customization, reports beyond the dashboard, custom fields, conditional business rules and workflow automation - then generalized across nearly every object with user & role management, a simple custom report builder and a dashboard KPI picker. The online demo was updated to mirror the same Admin panel in the browser.
- August 2026: Admin-defined Custom Objects shipped - a new record type an Administrator defines with no code, working automatically with custom fields, business rules and the report builder - followed by Custom Relationships between any two record types, a richer business rules engine (multi-condition, 10 operators), richer workflow automation (more triggers/actions, in-app notifications), custom field validation and capability flags, Windows task reminder notifications, and a session inactivity auto-lock, all mirrored in the online demo along with Reports, a no-code Screen layouts designer, and an Integrations admin section (a UI-only simulation, new to the product rather than a desktop port at the time).
- August 2026: Screen/App Builder shipped in full across four phases (named layouts with tabbed field sections assigned by role and Draft → Publish; multi-column sections with per-field width; custom-relationship related-lists placed on a specific tab; the same published layout also driving the read-only detail view) on both the desktop edition and the online demo, alongside Dashboard customization (KPI, chart and record-list widgets, named layouts assigned by role).
- August 2026: App Builder shipped - an Administrator groups any set of objects, their published screens, and one dashboard into a named, publishable app with its own icon, then grants it to roles or individual users as Viewer or Editor, enforced server-side on the desktop edition on every write including status-lifecycle actions. Shipped on desktop first and mirrored in the online demo (Admin → Apps, a sidebar App Switcher, and an app-scoped dashboard).
- August 2026: The Industry Data Model shipped - a versioned package manifest format installed into an existing workspace from a new Admin → App Catalog, reusing the workspace's existing Company/Contact/Task records instead of creating a parallel data model, with pre-install validation, an automatic safety backup, and a transactional install with rollback on failure. Ten reference packages shipped one at a time over the following weeks - Field Service, Property Management, Construction & Contractors, Professional Services, Dental/Clinic Practice Administration, Recruitment & Staffing, Real Estate Brokerage, Legal Practice, Nonprofit & Association Management, and Auto Repair & Service Garage - each reviewed and shipped with its own Rust core tests, reaching full parity in the online demo's own App Catalog. Per-app scoped automation followed, tagging business rules/workflows/dashboards an installed app creates so they stay visibly contained as more apps get installed.
- August 2026: Deployment Management shipped across four phases. Phase 1 added a read-only landing screen (Admin → Deployment Management) answering what's installed, what it created, and what it depends on. Phase 2 added a real Publisher registry with enforced namespace validation on package identifiers. Phase 3 added component-tagging across every admin-configurable artifact (not just what an install created), a synthetic "Local Workspace" row for everything built by hand, a real Export action producing a re-importable manifest, per-package Release history, and update-with-diff (Added/Modified/Removed) replacing the old "reinstalling an installed package is rejected outright" dead end. Phase 4 added named, scoped Solutions - a curated, versioned subset of components exportable on its own and importable into a second workspace through the ordinary App Catalog import flow - the build-in-test, promote-to-production pattern. All four phases shipped on the desktop edition and were mirrored in full in the online demo, including real Solution export.
- August 2026: The Integration Hub shipped on the desktop edition, attempting the full spec through its v1.1/v2 phasing best-effort: encrypted Connections (REST, SFTP, PostgreSQL, OData, SMTP, OAuth2), OpenAPI-imported Connectors usable as Workflow Automation actions, an API Access layer issuing hashed scoped keys against a generic REST API, HMAC-signed Webhooks with retry/backoff and delivery history, a generalized CSV Data Exchange wizard and reusable Mappings, read-only External Objects, Integration Jobs with a real background scheduler on the Team Workspace server, a unified execution log with real KPIs, and a Server-Sent-Events stream - proven with real local test doubles (an in-process SFTP server, a real local Postgres instance, mock OAuth2/SMTP/OData endpoints) wherever a live third-party service wasn't available, with mTLS left as the one explicitly deferred gap. The online demo's existing UI-only Integrations tab was relabeled and restructured (Overview, Integration Jobs, API Access, Connections, Webhooks & Events) to match the new terminology, staying an explicit simulation rather than claiming parity with the real desktop feature.
- September 2026: The AI & Agentic Layer shipped across five phases - a bring-your-own-key Chat Assistant and a native Model Context Protocol server & CLI; the AI Agent Foundry (named agents with persona, a per-tool Actions checklist, persistent Memory, a shared Skills library, and delegation); Orchestration (deterministic Pipelines, schedule/webhook/workflow-fired runs, one unified run history); a Unified AI Gateway (named AI Providers, per-agent primary/fallback/local-fallback routing with automatic failover, real token-usage accounting against System/Agent budgets, and DLP-driven forced air-gapping); and a Context Layer (real change-history for an agent's Memory, and a SQLite FTS5-backed ranked full-text search tool over Custom Object records - lexical `bm25()` relevance). All five phases shipped on the desktop edition and were mirrored in the online demo.
- September 2026: Five more pieces followed on the AI & Agentic Layer. Agent guardrails - an operational-boundary system-prompt injection an admin can edit, mirrored in the online demo, plus (desktop only, since it needs a real tool-calling loop) a genuinely code-enforced guard aborting the loop the moment the same call repeats 3 times in a row. Two more orchestration topologies - `consensus` and `peer_review` - alongside sequential, and human-in-the-loop approval gates extended from sequential Pipelines to every topology's own well-defined resume point (a consensus pipeline's synthesizer, a peer-review pipeline's reviewer every round) - both mirrored in the online demo, a synchronous `confirm()` dialog standing in for the desktop's real persisted pause-and-resume. Desktop only: declarative export/import of an agent or Skill as part of a Solution, reusing the existing Solution/package manifest mechanism; a real Evaluation Harness (`ai_eval_service`) grading golden test cases against an Agent or Pipeline's real response with an LLM-as-judge call; OTLP tracing on every run plus an on-demand push to a configured collector; an agent context primer (relationship metadata on `get_object_metadata`, a new `get_related_records` tool, and a new `get_platform_overview` tool); and Vector Search - embeddings-based semantic search over Custom Object records via the workspace's own already-configured OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini provider, stored as plain SQLite BLOBs and ranked by cosine similarity in Rust, not a bundled vector database.

## Core workflows

Customer records connect to contacts, opportunities, quotes, orders, invoices, contracts and tasks. Opportunities are optional for quotes. Quotes are optional for orders. Orders are optional for invoices. Relationship dropdowns are filtered by customer to preserve data integrity. Quotes, orders and invoices include product or service line items with quantities and pricing. That same connected model isn't fixed to these record types - an Administrator can add Custom Objects and link them into the graph with Custom Relationships, so nothing has to fall back to duplicated free text.

## Product principles

- Open source and transparent
- No licence activation
- Simple by default
- Modern user experience
- Local data ownership, now working in the early-access desktop edition
- Public roadmap, backlog and release notes

## Frequently asked

- **Is Lanesra OS free and open source?** Yes - MIT-licensed, the full source is on GitHub, no licence key or per-seat pricing.
- **Can I self-host it instead of using a cloud CRM?** Yes - the desktop edition runs fully offline against a local SQLite database, and Team Workspace mode lets a small team share one instance on their own network or infrastructure, with no Lanesra-run SaaS in between.
- **Is Lanesra OS only a CRM?** No - the same no-code platform underneath the CRM (Custom Objects, Relationships, Screen/App Builder, Business Rules, Workflow Automation, Dashboards, Reports) lets an Administrator build a completely different business app, or install one of 10 ready-made industry apps from the App Catalog - and its own AI agents run directly against that same data model.
- **Does it have a REST API and support webhooks?** Yes - the Integration Hub's generic `/api/v1/objects/...` REST API, OpenAPI-imported Connectors, and HMAC-signed outbound Webhooks, on the desktop edition's Team Workspace server.
- **How do I move customizations from a test workspace into production?** Deployment Management: curate a named, versioned Solution from any objects/fields/rules/workflows/screens you've built, export it, and import it into another workspace through the same validated App Catalog pipeline.
- **What's the difference between App Builder and the App Catalog?** App Builder packages your own hand-built objects into a named app; the App Catalog installs one of ten complete, ready-made industry apps someone else already built.
- **Does Lanesra OS use a vector database or embeddings for AI?** By default, no - ranked full-text search over Custom Object records uses SQLite's FTS5 `bm25()` lexical relevance. Desktop can optionally turn on Vector Search (Admin -> LLM & MCP -> Vector Search): real embeddings from the workspace's own already-configured OpenAI-compatible or Google Gemini provider (Anthropic has none), stored as plain SQLite BLOBs and ranked by cosine similarity in Rust - not a bundled vector database, and off until an admin opts in.
- **Can I bring my own LLM key, or run models locally?** Yes - the Unified AI Gateway routes to Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or Google Gemini with your own key (no markup or reselling), or to a fully local/air-gapped model, with automatic failover between tiers.
